name: Palm Leaf Text Line Segmentation Benchmark
description: Palm leaf manuscript is one of the oldest writing media used in South and Southeast Asia. Its use spanned from the medieval era into the nineteenth century, resulting in millions of manuscripts. These manuscripts encompass knowledge from various disciplines, and they deteriorated over time due to aging and environmental conditions. Hence, the digitization of palm leaf manuscripts is crucial for the preservation and dissemination of their rich knowledge. To improve the digitization performance, the line level segmentation and recognition are recommended over character level. Skewed lines, varied writing styles, and deterioration make line segmentation challenging, further compounded by the lack of diverse and publicly available datasets. To address this gap, we introduce LeafOCR-Line, a dataset for palm leaf text line segmentation, consisting of 1710 text line masked manuscripts with corresponding deterioration levels for each manuscript. Furthermore, extensive experiments demonstrate the high quality and practical utility of the proposed dataset. LeafOCR-Line will be publicly available as a valuable resource for advancing palm leaf manuscript digitization research.
evaluation_method: mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) / pixel-level F1 (often boundary-based F1 for line segmentation)
general_score_metric: mean IoU / pixel-level F1 (boundary F1 commonly reported for line segmentation)
reputation: A niche but valuable dataset within document analysis and cultural heritage communities for evaluating line segmentation on degraded palm-leaf manuscripts; adoption is moderate and mostly by specialized researchers.
notes: Specialized, non-LLM computer-vision benchmark with degraded handwritten documents and variable annotation granularity; dataset size and annotation noise can limit generalization. Not saturated and limited community coverage outside cultural-heritage research.
